findings.reason: The original standalone tile renders both formulas correctly but offers no visual comparison. A paired evaluation-and-summation schematic materially clarifies the differing group and lattice indices while making the common group-indexed output explicit. This is warranted explanatory diagram intake, not a defect in either displayed formula.

diagram_math_checks.data: Group row, fixed g in G
diagram_math_checks.check: Definition lines 31–34 give f:G→R^{C_in}, Psi:G→R^{C_in×C_out}. Since g^{-1}h belongs to G, both evaluations are defined. The product is a row vector of C_out coordinates, and its sum over h in G is precisely (C_Psi f)(g). No reordering or exchange of the factors is depicted.

diagram_math_checks.data: Lattice row, fixed g in G
diagram_math_checks.check: Definition lines 37–40 give f and Psi on Z². The given left action sends g^{-1}·x into Z², so the filter evaluation has the declared domain. Summation of the row-vector/matrix products over x in Z² is exactly (E_Psi f)(g). The left-action convention agrees with def-group-action-on-feature-maps.

diagram_math_checks.data: Four directed dataflow edges and six nodes
diagram_math_checks.check: Each row has only input-evaluations → indexed sum → output evaluation; no vertical edges or square assert equivariance or commutativity. Both output evaluations are at g in G. Channel multiplication is (1×C_in)(C_in×C_out)=1×C_out.

Remarks retain the Definition line 43 finite-support or coordinatewise absolute-convergence requirement. No finite-group, commutativity or stronger convergence condition is introduced. The rigorous definition is complete and independent of the schematic; this definition has no proof section.
